cards.intuition: Fill memory, sort that chunk, and spill one durable ordered run. Repeat instead of pretending storage offers RAM-like random access.
cards.formula: initial runs R = ceiling(N / usable run memory)
cards.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits

cards.intuition: Each merge level reads and writes the entire dataset. Larger practical fan-in reduces levels, but consumes more buffers and file handles.
cards.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits

cards.intuition: Treat each run as an immutable checkpoint: deterministic name, checksum, and publish-after-complete. Retries can reuse proven work.
cards.topic: External Merge Sort: Runs, Merging, and Memory Limits

cards.intuition: Only run heads can be the next global record. Keep those K competitors in a min-heap, emit one, and refill from its run.
cards.formula: merge N records from K runs in O(N log K) time and O(K) heap space

cards.intuition: Every run is sorted, so its head is its smallest remainder. The global minimum must therefore be among current heads.
cards.formula: emit minimum head, then advance only that head's run

cards.intuition: One huge merge saves a pass but may starve each stream of buffering or exhaust descriptors. Choose fan-in from measured I/O and resource limits.
cards.formula: trade full I/O passes against per-run buffers and stream count

cards.intuition: Tokenization emits document-grouped occurrences; sorting rearranges them into term-grouped postings with ordered documents and positions.
cards.formula: sort occurrence tuples by (term, doc_id, position)
cards.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem

cards.intuition: Once equal terms are adjacent, one pass can aggregate positions, gap-encode IDs, and finish each postings list before starting the next.
cards.formula: sorted occurrences → group term → encode postings → dictionary offset
cards.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem

cards.intuition: Create a sorted partial index within each memory-sized block, then merge partial indexes. Bounded memory becomes a normal design constraint.
cards.formula: parse block → sort → write run → merge runs
cards.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem

cards.intuition: New documents form small immutable sorted segments. Background merging controls segment count and physically applies deletions without rewriting everything per update.
cards.formula: new segment + background merge = incremental ordered index
cards.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem

cards.intuition: Increasing document IDs and positions turn into small gaps, while grouped terms avoid repeating keys. Construction order directly creates a compact serving layout.
cards.topic: Why Index Construction Is a Sorting Problem
